Eliza is the 'Lizzie Smith' who witnessed Mary's wedding in 1916. The household is gone from Carrickmore by 1911
Born 27 Feb 1886 at Cuttragh; father James Galligan, farmer; mother Rose formerly Rudden (Stradone district, entry 216)
Aged 15 in 1901, 25 and single in 1911

Daughter of John Smith, farmer, of Carrickmore (Ballyhaise DED — the Carrickmore north of Cavan town, not the others)
Married James Galligan in 1916, 'full age'

Farmer of Drumbar, Cavan; named as Margaret (Gretta) Brady's father on her 1949 marriage record

Re-reading the 1949 register: Drumbar, Cavan is Gretta's address as a domestic servant at the time of her marriage — her place of work, not necessarily her home. Michael's own townland is not given, so he could be anywhere in Cavan district
Born 19 Dec 1916 at Cuttragh, first child of James and Mary; father informant
A second James was born to the same parents in April 1920, which in Irish families almost always means the first had died
Born 15 Jan 1918 at Cuttragh; father James Galligan, farmer, informant
Born 29 Apr 1920 at 'Cuttra'; father James Galligan, farmer, informant

Lavey headstone (photo 84): 'Jim Galligan, Cornagall, Drung (formerly Cuttragh), died 9th March 2013' — with 'his grandfather James Galligan died 25th August 1928, his grandmother Rose (née Rudden) died 28th Nov. 1918'. A grandson of James and Rose, formerly of Cuttragh: this is Tom's brother, not Tom's son Jim
If the identification holds, he died fifteen days before Tom (24 March 2013) and moved from Cuttragh to Cornagall, in Drung parish to the north-east — Rose Rudden's home parish
Named on the Lavey headstone as son of James and Mary, died 15 Apr 2003 aged 86
No civil birth found under Galligan/Smith for 1917 in Cavan district — possibly registered late or under a variant

tom.pl: Cuttragh, Lavey; later Gortnakillew, Poles; Pullamore, Cavan
facts: Born 1 June 1923 at Cuttragh; father James Galligan, farmer; mother Mary formerly Smith (Stradone district, entry 413)
Brothers James (1916), John (c.1917) and James (1920); sister Rose (1918)
Married Margaret Brady at the Cathedral of SS Patrick and Felim, Cavan, 21 Feb 1949 — a farmer of Cuttragh; witnesses James Galligan and Frances McKeon
Daughter of Michael Brady, farmer, of Drumbar, Cavan — per her 1949 marriage record
Married Tom Galligan, 21 Feb 1949, Cavan Cathedral; 'full age', spinster, domestic
Died 16 January 2010 at home, Pullamore; notice names her Margaret (Gretta) Galligan née Brady; buried Killygarry

cathmc.pl: Hammondstown or Tonaghmore, Fore, Co. Westmeath
facts: Named as mother, 'Catherine McCormac formerly Reilly', on James's 1876 birth record
Census 1901: Catherine McCormack, 56, head of family, farmer, born Co. Westmeath, with son James, 25, at Hammondstown or Tonaghmore (house 3) — 'married', husband not present

thos.pl: Corbally and Hammondstown, Fore, Co. Westmeath
facts: Registered son James's birth himself in March 1876 as 'Terence McCormac, farmer, Hilltown', signing with his mark
The 1909 marriage record names James's father as 'Thos. McCormack' — a clerk's slip for Terence, since the father's own 1876 registration, the townland and the mother all match

Census 1901: Terence McCormack, 60, married, at Corbally (house 5) with his sister Bridget, 40 — while his wife Catherine ran the Hammondstown farm. Corbally was the family's home place; James's son Andy farmed it until 1991
Farmer, Ballinacree
Married Mary Gilsenan at Mount Nugent chapel, 27 Nov 1874, aged 28; father Michael McCormick, farmer
Census: 60 in 1901 with wife Maria 46; 69 and widowed in 1911 with daughter Julia

Aged 23 at her 1874 marriage; 46 in the 1901 census as 'Maria'

seanshine.pl: Inchintotane, Newmarket, Co. Cork → Adel, Oregon
facts: "Sean, 5, son" in the 1926 census at Inchantotane — the seventh of eight children then at home: Humphrey, Mollie, Patrick, Norah, William, Bridie, Sean and Thomas
Born June 1920 at Inchantotane, Newmarket, Co. Cork, to Jack (Patsy) Shine and Hannah McCarthy — the obituary says 12 June; the civil birth index (Kanturk district, mother McCarthy) says 14 June
Came to Oregon in 1948 — to the Guano Valley, then Warner Valley; took over his uncle Jack McCarthy's ranch at Adel and ranched for over 40 years
Born 1927 at Lakeview, Lake County, Oregon — probably named for her father's sister Laura A. Verling, who was at home in Newmarket in 1911

Named as John's father in his 2000 obituary

Birth year is an estimate, not from a record
Farmer at Meelin; named as Johanna McCarthy's father on her 1913 marriage record
His son Jack McCarthy had the ranch at Adel, Oregon that John (Seán) Shine later took over — so the McCarthys were in Oregon before the Shines
Agricultural labourer at Inchantotane; aged 74 in 1901 and 83 in 1911; spoke Irish and English; could not read
Married Margaret about 1859 — 52 years married in 1911, 12 children born, 10 living
Sons James (b. c.1872) and Patrick (b. c.1880) at home in 1901; James still with them in 1911
Aged 64 in 1901 (housekeeper, could read and write) and 73 in 1911; Irish and English
Mother of 12 children, 10 living in 1911
At home with his parents in 1901 (aged 29) and 1911 (39); still at Inchantotane, unmarried, aged 55, in his brother Jack's household in 1926

Aged 21, farmer's daughter of Meelin, when she married John P. Shine at Rock Chapel on 29 April 1913; her father William McCarthy, farmer

bartv.pl: Heathfield Towers, Youghal → Oxclose, Newmarket, Co. Cork
facts: Naval surgeon; lived to 96
Married first Mary Walsh of Youghal (d. 1844, aged 30) — children Bartholomew and Catherine died young; Mary married Francis Power of Roskeen, near Mallow
Married second Sabina, daughter of Walter Hervey Kavanagh of Ballyhale, Co. Kilkenny — children Walter Kavanagh Verling MD and Arabella, who died young

Newmarket Church of Ireland graveyard: 'Here lieth the remains of Bartholomew Verling, he died at Oxclose July 20th 1865 aged 12 yrs; also Arabella Verling, she died at Queenstown Dec'r 4th aged 19 yrs; they were the children of Batholomew Verling Esqr of Oxclose and his wife Sabina Kavanagh'
Birth year is an estimate, worked back from her son Walter's birth about 1850, not from a record
Daughter of Walter Hervey Kavanagh of Ballyhale, Co. Kilkenny (d. 1853); the published pedigree traces her line to Morgan Kavanagh of Ballyhale and Castle Morres and Lady Frances Butler
Her son carried both names: Walter Kavanagh Verling
Birth year is an estimate, worked back from his son Bartholomew's birth in 1797, not from a record
Named as Dr Bartholomew Verling's father in the published pedigree

The 1916 Verling pedigree calls him 'Staff Captain RN', son of Bartholomew Verling of Cove and Anne O'Cullinane, husband of Anne Ronayne of Ballinacrusha, Cuskinny, and brother of John Verling — which would make his children (Bartholomew, Fr Patrick Verling PP of Charleville, and Mary, wife of Capt. Leary RN) first cousins of James Roche Verling
Birth year is an estimate, not from a record
Named as Dr Bartholomew Verling's mother; sister of John Roche of Aghada's wife or a Roche by marriage — the pedigree calls Bartholomew John Roche's nephew through her
Birth year is an estimate, not from a record
Of Ballyhale, Co. Kilkenny; died 1853 according to the Verling pedigree

walterv.pl: Oxclose (Springfield Lodge), Garraunawarrig Upper, Newmarket, Co. Cork
facts: Son of Dr Bartholomew Verling, naval surgeon, and Sabina Kavanagh of Ballyhale, Co. Kilkenny; the family seat was Oxclose, also called Springfield Lodge, outside Newmarket
Married Mary Malpas, born in England — the published pedigree says nine sons and a daughter; the 1911 census, which the couple filled in themselves, says nineteen children born
Physician and surgeon in Newmarket, Co. Cork — 'the family was prominent there'; born Co. Cork about 1850
Daughter of a Mr Malpas, according to the Verling pedigree; born in England about 1854; Church of Ireland, while her husband and children were Catholic
Mother of 19 children, 15 of them living in 1911, after 37 years of marriage

fverling.pl: Newmarket, Co. Cork → Drews Gap, Lakeview, Oregon
facts: Married Mary Josephine O'Keeffe in San Francisco on 18 June 1916; a first son, Walter Francis, was born there in 1917 (FamilySearch shared tree)
Born in Newmarket, Co. Cork, 3 August 1881 — the same town the Shines came from, and the same birthday as Shane Galligan, exactly a century apart
Son of the town doctor, Walter Kavanagh Verling, and one of a family of nineteen or more children (the obituary says 21; the 1911 census says 19 born, 15 living)
Born in Co. Cork, 15 April 1895; a brother Tim O'Keeffe and a sister Julia Doherty were still in Cork when she died
Married Francis Verling in San Francisco; a Lake County resident from 1920
Widowed in 1929 with seven children and a newborn; married Patrick W. Fitzgerald (1904–1994) in 1937

howardh.pl: Vernonia, Oregon; later Sisters, Oregon; Longview and Vancouver, Washington
facts: Born 6 March 1930 and died 20 March 2020, aged 90 — the dates printed with his obituary in the Longview Daily News, 31 March 2020
The Columbian death notices, 21 March 2020: 'Howard K. Hopkins, 90, Vancouver, died March 20, 2020', in the care of All County Cremation and Burial Services
The obituary opens: he 'lived to be 90 years old, which was not enough' — the rest is behind the newspaper's paywall and has not been read, so his parents and birthplace are still unknown

Son of William T. Hopkins, born in Wales, and Marie (Mariah), born in England; a boy of 10 at Elwood, Indiana, in 1910 with brothers Archibald and Edward and sisters Gladys, Mary and Florence
Married Rose A. Tucker Ellis at Vancouver, Washington, on 3 November 1928
A likely match, not yet proven: wife of Marcus A. Hopkins in the 1950 census of Oakridge, Oregon, aged 46, born Nebraska
Mother of Howard, 19, and Stanley E. in that household
Born in Wales about 1868, both parents Welsh; head of the household at Elwood, Indiana, in 1910, aged 42
Elwood was a tinplate town that drew many Welsh tinworkers in the 1890s
Named as Marcus's father on the 1928 marriage record and in his Social Security file
Born in England about 1878, both parents English; wife of William T. Hopkins at Elwood in 1910, aged 32

places.t: The Galligan home farm from at least 1901. Tom was born here in 1923.
Where Tom and Gretta farmed and raised Jim, John and Rose after 1949.
Gretta's home place in 1949; her father Michael Brady farmed here. Which Drumbar is still to be confirmed.
The chapel where James Galligan married Mary Smith in February 1916.
Mary Smith's home townland in Ballyhaise DED, where four Smith farms stood in 1901.
Rose Rudden's home townland; the Ruddens were still farming here in 1901.
Where James Galligan married Rose Rudden in February 1882.
The McCormack home place: Terence was here in 1901, and his grandson Andy farmed it until 1991.
The McCormack farm. Catherine was head here in 1901; Jimmy was born at Hilltown in 1914.
SS Patrick and Felim — Tom and Gretta married here on 21 February 1949.
Where Tom (2013) and Gretta (2010) are buried.
The Galligans of Cuttragh are buried here.
Tom and Gretta's last home, on the Dublin Road.
The village and abbey at the heart of the McCormack home parish.
Three generations of McCormicks farmed here; Brigid was born here in 1878 and married here in 1909.
Andrew McCormick married Mary Gilsenan here in 1874.
Granny McCormack's home: the Gilsenan farm where Bridget was born in 1912.
The Donnelly farm, in Lickbla parish: Francis Donnelly held it in Griffith's Valuation c.1854; his son Patrick, 72, was a widower here in 1901.

The Early home: Elizabeth was "of Caralana" on her 1870 marriage record; Michael Early held land at Corralanna in Griffith's Valuation, and Earlys were still there in 1901. Elizabeth married Patrick Donnelly at Street chapel in 1870.
Where Tom's brother Jim Galligan lived later, if the Lavey headstone is his; he died in March 2013.
Where Michael Gilsenan married Mary Donnelly, 27 July 1905.
Home of the Plunketts, who connect somewhere to Granny McCormack.
Where Chris (Brendan) and Vera McCormack's children Sarah, Stephen and Fiona were born — from Shane.
Where John and Margaret raised their family.
Where Fr Pat McCormack, Jimmy's brother, served as a priest and died.
Inchantotane townland, outside Newmarket in Duhallow, north-west Cork — Shines have farmed and laboured here since before the Famine; John (Seán) was born here in 1920.
Laura Verling's home town; her parents ranched at Drews Gap to the west. She and John married here in 1958; Laura, Francis and Mary Josephine are buried in Sunset Park Cemetery.
Home of the Kavanaghs of Ballyhale, Sabina Kavanagh's people.
The Verlings were a Cove of Cork family — the town's Dr James Roche Verling sailed with Napoleon to St Helena in 1815.

Oxclose, or Springfield Lodge — Dr Bartholomew Verling's house and then his son Dr Walter's, on the edge of Newmarket, where nineteen Verling children were raised — a mile or two from the Shines at Inchantotane. Francis left here for Oregon about 1900.
Where Howard and Velma Hopkins raised their family.
Where Howard Hopkins and Velma Klein may have grown up — to be confirmed.
Where Velma lives today, and where Howard died in March 2020.
The Warner Valley ranch where John (Seán) Shine worked for forty years; he is buried in Adel Cemetery.
Where Kelley was born in 1987.
Home of the Oregon branch of the family.
